nodes.label: Tests for the basket screen: the matrix, the scenarios, and the key bindings.  T
Fix what basket.optimize hands the screen instead of relying on the search.
Push the basket and wait until its first read has landed.
A site with no prices must be visibly empty, not invisibly absent.      Sourcing
A site nobody scans cannot be part of a comparison of today's prices.
A sold-out listing must not win a comparison it cannot actually fill.      It is
Two sizes of one perfume are two rows with two prices, never one.      The matri
The matrix is a price list, the scenario is a bill.      Multiplying the quantit
The age column exists to be glanced at, so it is phrased, not printed.
A row is only as fresh as the oldest price it is comparing.      Reporting the n
The warning has to stay quiet when nothing is wrong, or it gets ignored.
A partial total is cheaper for the wrong reason, so it is never mixed in.      S
"Add one more and shipping is free" is the whole point of this screen.
A threshold of NULL means there is no gap to close, at any subtotal.      Printi
A "3% off by bank transfer" note changes which total is really cheapest.
A blank screen with no explanation reads as a broken screen.
A row of nothing but dashes needs saying out loud, not leaving to be read.
Quantity is what turns a price list into a bill, so it is editable here.
Removal has its own key, so "-" must never be a surprise delete.      The quanti
The list is edited here, not only on the search screen.
Refresh is the most expensive thing the app does, so it reports itself.      The
A suspect site keeps serving its last good price, and that price is a lie.
An empty answer is evidence of absence, so the stored price has to go.      late
A shop that dropped one decant is still telling the truth about the rest.      T
The pacing lives inside a single run_site call, so overlapping them loses it.
The basket is pushed over the search screen, so the scan survives the trip.
The block must never be mistaken for a mathematically proven answer.      optimi
The whole point of the block is telling the user how much splitting saves.
A split that costs more must read as a warning, never as a suggestion.      The
A partial site's total is cheap for the wrong reason: it skipped a line.      Co
A comparison against nothing would look like a number, not an absence.      When
None means no combination of sites can fill the basket at all.      Showing an e
Nothing to buy means nothing to split, so the block has no reason to show.
A one-leg plan is the best single site restated, and must read that way.      Pr
A truncated search has to say so, or a narrowed answer reads as complete.      o
